question: What is a core goal of immunization within Primary Health Care?

options.A: To treat acute bacterial infections in children
options.B: To replace the need for clean water and nutrition
options.C: To interrupt transmission of vaccine-preventable diseases
options.D: To completely eliminate all known human illnesses

explanation: The main purpose of immunization in public health is to prevent specific infectious diseases and stop them from spreading in communities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h1)

question: Why does a drop in immunization coverage pose a major danger to a community?

options.A: It leads to severe outbreaks of preventable diseases
options.B: It causes immediate antibiotic resistance in infants
options.C: It increases the cost of treating chronic genetic disorders
options.D: It permanently ruins the cold chain storage equipment

explanation: When too many children miss their shots, community immunity falls, allowing dangerous infections to return and spread rapidly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h1)

question: Which of the following is a common logistical barrier to immunization in rural areas?

options.A: Too many nurses working in primary health centers
options.B: Poor road networks and long geographical distances
options.D: Excessive availability of cold storage boxes

explanation: Bad roads and remote locations make it very hard for health workers to transport vaccines and for families to reach clinics. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h2)

question: How do rumors and misinformation about vaccine safety affect community coverage?

options.A: They increase caregiver hesitancy and lead to missed vaccinations
options.B: They force health workers to improve the cold chain system
options.C: They have no real impact on routine immunization numbers
options.D: They make parents bring their children to the clinic much earlier

explanation: When parents hear false safety claims, fear stops them from allowing their children to receive life-saving vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h2)

question: Who are key partners for nurses when mobilizing a local community for immunization?

options.A: National security forces and immigration officers
options.B: Local leaders, religious figures, and women's groups

explanation: Working with trusted local and religious figures helps nurses gain the confidence of community members. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h3)

question: Why is it important to use local languages and traditional communication channels for immunization campaigns?

options.A: It prevents the government from spending money on printed books
options.B: It is required to qualify for international medical grants
options.C: It stops people from visiting traditional bone setters
options.D: It ensures the message is clearly understood and trusted by residents

explanation: Using familiar languages and traditional methods like town criers breaks down communication barriers and reduces fear. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain in immunization programs?

options.A: To speed up the delivery of medical supplies to large cities
options.B: To keep vaccines within safe temperature ranges so they remain potent
options.C: To store expired medications safely away from patients
options.D: To freeze liquid vaccines completely solid before use

explanation: The cold chain protects heat-sensitive vaccines from losing their medical effectiveness before they reach the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h4)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility regarding vaccine storage at a health facility?

options.A: Repairing broken compressors in refrigerator units
options.B: Checking and logging refrigerator temperatures twice daily
options.C: Testing the chemical composition of each vaccine vial
options.D: Ordering new vaccine stocks directly from foreign factories

explanation: Nurses must monitor and record storage temperatures regularly to catch equipment failures before vaccines are ruined. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of mobile vaccination clinics and outreach services?

options.A: To bring immunization services closer to remote or hard-to-reach populations
options.B: To provide emergency surgical care during disease outbreaks
options.C: To reduce the number of trained nurses needed in clinics
options.D: To replace permanent hospitals in major cities

explanation: Outreach services overcome distance barriers by bringing vaccines directly to communities that cannot travel to health centers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h5)

question: A community located twenty kilometers from the nearest health post has very low immunization rates due to bad roads. What is the most effective intervention?

options.A: Close the primary health post and relocate staff to the city
options.B: Send written warning letters to parents who miss clinic dates
options.C: Organize scheduled mobile outreach vaccination clinics for the village
options.D: Wait for parents to bring their children when roads are dry

explanation: Taking the services directly to remote communities through mobile clinics solves the geographical barrier causing low coverage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h5)

question: What defines an immunization 'defaulter' child?

options.A: A child who experienced a severe allergic reaction to a vaccine
options.B: A child who completed all required immunizations ahead of time
options.C: A child who received an initial dose but missed subsequent scheduled doses
options.D: A child who has never received any vaccine at all

explanation: A defaulter started their immunization schedule but failed to return for booster or subsequent doses on time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h6)

question: Why is it important for nurses to review immunization registers regularly?

options.A: To calculate monthly staff salary and allowances
options.B: To identify children who have missed scheduled doses and need tracking
options.C: To find out which vaccine brand is most expensive
options.D: To report families to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Regular register checks help nurses spot missing children early so they can organize follow-up visits before outbreaks happen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h6)

question: Which of the following best describes inter-sectoral collaboration in immunization?

options.A: Partnering with schools, religious bodies, and local leaders to boost coverage
options.B: Leaving all public health work entirely to the central government
options.C: Working exclusively with doctors inside major hospital wards
options.D: Buying vaccines from international suppliers without local input

explanation: Inter-sectoral collaboration brings different community groups together to work toward shared public health goals. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h7)

question: How does partnering with schools help improve childhood immunization rates?

options.A: It forces teachers to administer complex injectable vaccines
options.B: It allows health workers to check vaccination cards and catch up on missed doses
options.C: It ensures that children never catch common colds at home
options.D: It replaces the need for infant clinics at primary health centers

explanation: Schools provide a structured setting where health workers can easily review children's immunization records and administer catch-up vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h7)

question: What is a primary tool used by nurses to record daily immunizations at the clinic level?
explanation: Tally sheets and registers are standard tools nurses use every day to keep a precise count of every vaccine given. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h8)

question: Why is accurate data management critical for preventing vaccine stockouts?

options.A: It helps health workers calculate exact needs and order correct quantities
options.B: It prevents refrigerators from losing power during storms
options.C: It stops patients from asking for unnecessary medications
options.D: It proves to international donors that nurses are working hard

explanation: Good records show how many doses are actually used, allowing clinics to order enough stock without running out or wasting supplies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h8)
